Patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions to mirikizumab or any of its excipients should not use this medication. 3. Currently available data from case reports on the use of mirikizumab in pregnant women are insufficient to assess the risk of major birth defects, miscarriage, or other adverse maternal or fetal outcomes associated with the drug. 4. Monoclonal antibodies, including mirikizumab, can be actively transported across the placenta, potentially causing immunosuppression in infants exposed in utero. 5. There is no data available regarding the presence of mirikizumab in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. 6. Endogenous maternal IgG and monoclonal antibodies are known to be transferred into human breast milk. 7. The effects of local gastrointestinal exposure and limited systemic exposure to mirikizumab in breastfed infants remain unknown. 8. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk, and the drug is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy. 9. When preparing for intravenous administration, the time required to flush the IV line is in addition to the minimum 30-minute infusion time. 10. Subcutaneous injection sites include the abdomen, thigh, and the back of the upper arm. 11. Rotate injection sites with each administration and avoid injecting into areas where the skin is tender, bruised, erythematous, or indurated. 12.
